dispositions.rationale: No responsible complete value is asserted. The new search does find ordinary response vocabulary: itasa itak / itasaytak. The remaining ambiguity is how to compose an unambiguous network response containing Commons metadata and to make its accumulated downloaded byte size the bounded object. The existing autosave phrase iyanu newa oruspe (イヤヌ ネワ オルㇱペ) is a context-specific catalogue candidate, not independently established generic metadata terminology. Combining it with a response noun and a generic size term could still read as a limit on descriptive/settings text. The existing pororu / ポロル and pakno kasu / パㇰノ カス strings remain unaccepted candidate evidence. Commons must remain literally Commons. Both Ainu script variants remain unresolved together, with the same intended meaning: the Commons metadata response exceeds the allowed response byte size.
dispositions.review_limit: Insufficient competence to validate a complete Ainu technical sentence, its compound/relative-clause attachment, and idiomatic abstract size comparison. A competent Ainu reviewer should choose a metadata paraphrase and either validate a network extension of itasa itak or use a clear received-data paraphrase, then back-translate the complete sentence. The Kana spelling must be checked against the chosen Latin wording and dialect; do not mechanically transliterate an unvalidated draft. This is a bounded unresolved result, not a claim that the language lacks an expression.

dispositions.value: Commons ke chûng-ki chṳ̂-liau fì-tap ke thai-se chhêu chhut sông-han.
dispositions.rationale: Source-assisted, low-confidence proposal in intended Sixian Pha̍k-fa-sṳ: the size of the Commons metadata response exceeds the upper limit. The MOE Hakka dictionary gives 回答 with Sixian fi11 dab2 in the answer/respond sense; independently published Hakka prose and the Hakka Bible attest the PFS form fì-tap. This supplies a grounded response/answer candidate rather than guessing the reading of 回應. The metadata, genitive, size, exceed and upper-limit vocabulary is retained from the existing PFS catalogue only as candidate material. The subject is response size, not metadata-field length, response count or timeout. Commons remains literal. No 2 MiB figure is added because the English UI string does not contain it.
dispositions.review_limit: Not competent-native acceptance. A Sixian PFS reviewer must validate the whole sentence, all tones and word boundaries, the catalogue metadata term, and the extension of ordinary answer/response fì-tap to an HTTP response. This deliberately uses 回答 rather than the separate hak-Hant-TW draft’s 回應; the pair needs joint editorial review before adoption. The primary MOE and FHL entries were inspected in indexed search excerpts; direct opening returned errors, so they establish constituent evidence only. I have not found primary technical Hakka evidence for this complete compound or sentence.

dispositions.value: 戟 𡱩 返回 超 與 料 𧵑 Commons 越 過 界限.
dispositions.rationale: Low-confidence Hán/Nôm proposal, with explicit intended Quốc ngữ reading: Kích thước phản hồi siêu dữ liệu của Commons vượt quá giới hạn. Back-translation: the size of the Commons metadata response exceeds the limit. The source dictionary directly lists the written compounds for response/return, size, data and limit, and the component readings for the remaining words. Modern Vietnamese API documentation independently uses phản hồi for a JSON/HTTP response; a Vietnamese ministry article uses siêu dữ liệu for metadata. The bounded subject is response size, never a metadata field or text length. Existing catalogue spacing and Commons are retained. The technical sense is a proposed modern usage in Hán/Nôm, not claimed historical attestation.
dispositions.review_limit: Not competent Hán/Nôm acceptance. A competent reviewer must read and back-translate the complete sentence, assess whether 返回 is understood as the intended technical response rather than merely returning, and validate the modern metadata compound, spacing and byte-size interpretation. The Hán/Nôm source is a revival group’s own orthographic reference, not proof of a universally accepted historical or modern standard. Character readings plus modern Quốc ngữ terminology do not independently certify the composed Hán/Nôm sentence. No visual rendering or native review has been done.
